question: Has the collective discussed Diginex's path to profitability given the M&A spend?

beats.line: The collective hasn't discussed this much recently, so this view draws on outside sources.
beats.headline: OUTSIDE SOURCES
beats.action: A folded paper document unfolds onto a cream chip and settles flat.

beats.line: Diginex's profitability hinges on a classic merger problem: near-term margin squeeze, longer-term operating leverage.
beats.headline: INTEGRATION TAX
beats.action: The document splits into two torn arrows, one bending down, one climbing right.

beats.line: The company is in active integration mode across four acquisitions.
beats.headline: 4 ACQUISITIONS
beats.action: The arrows flatten into a base as four paper blocks drop on and lock together.

beats.line: In the six months to September, general costs climbed three point four million to eight point one million dollars.
beats.headline: G&A $8.1M
beats.action: The block row stacks upward into one tall paper bar that holds at the top of frame.

beats.line: Two point two million came from deal diligence and legal work — about twenty-seven percent of the increase.
beats.headline: 27% ONE-OFF
beats.action: A shaded wedge slides across the tall bar, cutting a marked slice that stays lit.

beats.line: The Resulticks deal is the largest and most complex, and likely extends the integration tax into twenty twenty-seven.
beats.headline: INTO 2027
beats.action: The wedge unrolls into a calendar strip that stretches out past the frame edge.

beats.line: Profitability needs revenue growing thirty to fifty percent while costs stay flat or grow in single digits.
beats.headline: +30–50% YOY
beats.action: From the strip a paper arrow climbs steeply while a flat paper line holds level beneath it.

beats.line: It needs cross-sell too; without it, you get two siloed businesses with duplicate overhead.
beats.headline: CROSS-SELL
beats.action: The arrow splits into two paper boxes; a ribbon reaches between them and pulls taut.

beats.line: Diginex has signalled focus on Brazil's seventy-seven billion dollar sustainability market as a new revenue stream.
beats.headline: $77B MARKET
beats.action: The ribbon loops around a cutout map shape that lifts and holds centre frame.

beats.line: The next two to three earnings reports must show it — until then, profitability is a narrative.
beats.headline: NEXT 2–3 REPORTS
beats.action: The map folds into three report pages; a paper hand enters and points at the last one.
